/itineraryStops/4/description.source_en:
⟦G1⟧ (인사동) is Seoul's premier traditional crafts and cultural street — a pedestrian-friendly main road plus a network of side alleys lined with antique shops, calligraphy supplies, hanji (mulberry paper) workshops, ceramic galleries, traditional teahouses, and Korean souvenir vendors. 

Originally settled in the late Joseon era as a residential district for retired aristocrats and government officials, ⟦G1⟧ became a center for traditional Korean cultural commerce in the 20th century and remains the city's go-to district for hanbok accessories, traditional tea sets, and museum-quality calligraphy supplies. 

The signature landmark is **Ssamzigil** — a 4-story spiral cultural complex at the heart of ⟦G1⟧ with 70+ small craft shops, art galleries, cafes, and a rooftop terrace; designed in 2004 around a continuous spiral ramp that takes shoppers from ground to roof in a single seamless walk. 

Other ⟦G1⟧ specialties: **traditional teahouses** (jeontongchatjip — try Mokyeon for omija five-flavor tea or Suyeonsanbang for the classical experience); **hanji paper workshops** (handmade Korean mulberry paper folding/stamping demos); **ceramic galleries** showing Goryeo celadon and Joseon white porcelain; and **Balwoo Gongyang** — Korea's only Michelin-starred Buddhist temple-cuisine restaurant, run by the Jogye Order (next to ⟦G0⟧, 5 min walk). 

The street is cleared of vehicles for pedestrian-only access on weekends (Sat-Sun). ⟦G1⟧'s main pedestrian street stretches **~700 meters** from Anguk Station to Jongno-3-ga, with branch alleys hosting the densest concentration of traditional-craft vendors in central Seoul.

/itineraryStops/5/description.source_en:
Return drive **60-90 minutes** from central Seoul back to the **Incheon Cruise Terminal at Songdo**, arriving with a 60-90 min buffer before typical **19:00-20:00 all-aboard times**. Route runs via the **Incheon-Seoul Expressway and Yeongjong Bridge** in reverse, with traffic conditions typically lighter than the morning commute. 

Drop-off direct at the terminal curbside — followed by Korean immigration re-entry to the cruise ship (usually fast at this time of day). Confirm your ship's specific all-aboard time at the terminal before disembarking the van — traffic delays are rare on this expressway but the **90-min cushion** is the prudent buffer.
